➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

TON DNS Summer (Part 1)

As we predicted, the hype around TON DNS has begun. The hype began with Four-Digit domains (hereinafter referred to as 4N domains). People are "burning" their 100 TON on the TON DNS smart contract and transferring this value to NFTs (similar to Banksy's work). 

On February 13, the last domain from the Club 100 (0074.ton), was minted, on February 17, the thousandth domain (5755.ton), and on February 28, the last domain from the 1k Club (0863.ton).

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

8. Repeating the success of ENS, this time in the form of a utility — a shell in Telegram (because TON DNS renewal costs pennies, compared to $160 per year for a 4-digit ENS).

WIKILEAKS NUCLEAR BOMBSHELL: Julian Assange Says CIA Planned to KIDNAP and ASSASSINATE Him — Wife and 6-Month-Old Son TARGETED, DNA Sought From Baby’s Nappy — Clinton “DRONE THIS GUY?” Claim Resurfaces

Julian Assange has given a stark account of what he says unfolded after WikiLeaks published material that powerful institutions wanted buried. He says the CIA drew up plans to kidnap and assassinate him inside the Ecuadorian Embassy in London, authorized action against his European colleagues, and subjected those around him to theft, hacking, and the planting of false information.

Assange says the campaign did not stop with him. A CIA asset was permanently assigned to track his wife. Instructions were given to obtain DNA from his six-month-old son’s nappy. A baby’s diaper. A child’s genetic material. That is the allegation he places on the record: an intelligence operation that reached into his family after WikiLeaks exposed files tied to Hillary Clinton, John Podesta, Barack Obama, and other figures who wanted the leaks contained.

The Clinton remark now resurfacing is the line attributed to her while officials hunted ways to cut off the cables and limit the damage: “Can’t we just drone this guy?” In that telling, WikiLeaks was not treated as journalism. Assange was treated as a problem to be removed.

The larger question attached to his account is familiar to anyone who watched the war on Donald Trump. If agencies and political operators would plan a kidnapping, hunt a wife, seek an infant’s DNA, and float a drone strike to stop exposure, why assume they would stop short of a fabricated Russia narrative, the silencing of Seth Rich, lawfare, bankruptcy schemes, or election interference when their grip on power was at risk?

💬 Iran, Eurasian Economic Union discuss expanding trade

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Iran’s economy minister holds talks with senior officials of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) in Moscow on accelerating trade transactions between the two sides and strengthening Iran’s presence in the bloc’s market of more than 180 million people.

Seyed Ali Madanizadeh, Iran’s minister of economic affairs and finance, met with Bagit Jan Sagintayev, chairman of the executive board of the Eurasian Economic Commission, the EAEU’s highest-ranking official on Monday. During the meeting, the two sides emphasized their joint determination to develop cooperation. Before the meeting, Madanizadeh held separate talks with Andrey Slepnev, the EAEU’s minister for trade, and a number of officials from the bloc. The meeting focused on the course of cooperation between Iran and the EAEU following the implementation of their free trade agreement. Slepnev referred to the planned second meeting of the Iran-EAEU working group, which is scheduled to be held in Tehran in the coming months, and expressed hope that the upward trend in trade between the sides would continue. Iran’s ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali and Mehdi Heidari, deputy economy minister and head of the Organization for Investment and Economic and Technical Assistance of Iran, accompanied Madanizadeh during the meetings. The free trade agreement between Iran and the EAEU came into effect in May 2025 after completing the legal procedures in the signatory countries. Under the agreement, customs duties on 87% of goods traded between the sides were eliminated. The agreement has opened the way for Iranian goods to enter the markets of the EAEU’s more than 180 million people, while businesses from the bloc’s five member states have gained the same opportunity to trade with Iran. Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia are members of the EAEU, while Iran is an observer member of the bloc. Madanizadeh arrived in Moscow on Sunday for bilateral and multilateral talks. On Monday evening, Madanizadeh attended a meeting with Iranian traders and economic activists living in Russia, where he listened to their concerns and discussed their business activities.
​
On Tuesday, he met with his Russian counterpart to discuss the expansion of economic relations, a meeting he said had been accompanied by “good openings” in trade and economic relations.
